column1: # Hebrew (he) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); the translation lists the
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Text is stored in logical (reading) order; the UI draws it right to left (see rtl_text.rs).
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Hebrew computing vocabulary (שכבה, טשטוש, בחירה ...). No proprietary localisation resource,
# string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add entries the same way.
# Product and technology names (PhotoCraft, ArtCraft, OpenType, CMYK, Lab ...) stay in Latin
# letters; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept.
